critique_history.assessment:
- The back is dominated by large smooth oval panels instead of dense feather texture; cover the full body and crown with smaller overlapping feathers.
- Wing feathers form stiff vertical curtains and appear poorly integrated; reshape both folded wings into attached tapered masses with layered contour-following rows.
- The chest feathers resemble large scales; make them finer, narrower, and more densely overlapped.
- The beak is too long and straight; shorten it and give the tip a subtle downward curve.

- The oversized smooth crown forms a detached-looking helmet; remove it and blend gray crown feathers directly into the head.
- Wings are thick rectangular slabs; reshape them into tapered, body-hugging folded wings.
- Body and head feathers read as raised circular scales rather than overlapping plumage; use smaller pointed, layered feather patches.
- The rear silhouette is overly cylindrical; soften the neck-body transition and taper the lower body.
